cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is about to die. Before his death, Moses the man of God speaks a blessing over the Israelites. It's his last big speech, friend, and the man spends it blessing everybody else.

Before he blesses a single tribe, Moses starts with the LORD showing up for His people. The LORD came from Sinai, dawned from Seir and shone forth from Mount Paran, with flaming fire at His right hand.

cards.question: After that blazing picture, Moses talks right to the LORD. What does Moses say about the LORD and the people?

cards.text: Surely You love the people, Moses says. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, I would have CRIED at "Surely You remember the stamper."

cards.question: Moses says the holy ones sit at the LORD's feet, and each one receives His words. Those words are the ___ that Moses gave us.
Moses says the LORD became King in Jeshurun when the tribes of Israel came together.
Now Moses blesses the tribes one by one, starting with the tribe of Reuben. Moses says Reuben's men will be few.

cards.text: Next up, the tribe of Judah. Moses asks the LORD to hear the cry of Judah and bring him to his people.

cards.question: Judah defends his cause with his own hands. Moses asks the LORD to be his ___ against his foes.

cards.text: Then the tribe of Levi. Moses asks the LORD to give His Thummim and His Urim to Levi, His godly one.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD tested Levi and contested him at the waters. Where did that happen?

cards.text: Then Moses says Levi said of his father and mother, "I do not consider them." He disregarded his brothers and didn't even know his own sons.

cards.question: Moses says Levi disregarded his brothers and didn't know his own sons. Why?

answers.text: He kept God's word and covenant
He wanted a bigger share of land
He was angry with his brothers

cards.question: Moses says Levi will teach the LORD's ordinances to Jacob and His law to Israel.

cards.text: Levi will serve at the altar too, and Moses asks the LORD to bless his substance and accept the work of his hands. Teaching AND the altar, friend, and I can't run ONE oven without singeing my mustache.

cards.question: Next is the tribe of Benjamin. Moses calls him the beloved of the LORD, shielded by God all day long and resting upon His shoulders. How does Moses want Benjamin to rest in Him?

cards.text: Then the tribe of Joseph, and Moses goes BIG: may his land be blessed with dew from heaven, deep waters below, the harvest from the sun and the best of the ancient mountains. That's not a blessing, friend, that's a whole TOPPING BAR.

cards.question: On top of all that, Moses names someone's favor to rest on Joseph's head. Whose favor is it?

answers.text: Him who dwelt in the burning bush
The king who ruled over Egypt
The elders who sat at the gate

cards.question: Moses says Joseph's majesty is like a firstborn bull, with horns like those of a wild ox. With those horns, he will ___ the nations.

cards.text: Ephraim and Manasseh are Joseph's two sons, and each has a tribe named after him. Such are the myriads of Ephraim, Moses says, and such are the thousands of Manasseh.
Now Moses blesses the tribes of Zebulun and Issachar together. Rejoice, Zebulun, in your journeys, he says, and Issachar, in your tents.

cards.question: Moses says Zebulun and Issachar will call the peoples to a mountain. What will they offer there?
Moses says Zebulun and Issachar will feast on the abundance of the seas.

cards.text: Next is the tribe of Gad, and Moses says blessed is he who enlarges the domain of Gad. Friend, the only domain I ever enlarged was the flour cloud around my counter.

cards.question: Moses pictures Gad lying down like a lion that tears off an arm or a head. What kind of tribe does that picture describe?
Moses says Gad chose the best land and came with the leaders of the people. What did Gad carry out for Israel?
The tribe of Dan gets the shortest blessing yet. Moses calls Dan a lion's cub leaping out of Bashan.

cards.text: Then the tribe of Naphtali. Moses says Naphtali is abounding with favor, full of the blessing of the LORD.

cards.question: Moses says Naphtali will take possession of the mountains and the north.

cards.text: Last tribe on the list: Asher. And Moses saves a big one for the end.

cards.question: Moses' blessing for Asher, the last tribe he names, aims high. What does Moses want for Asher?

answers.text: To be the most blessed of sons
To rule over all the tribes
To be the first in battle

cards.text: Moses goes on: may Asher be the most favored among his brothers and dip his foot in oil. I once dipped my whole gold base in cookie dough, and NOBODY called that a blessing.
Then Moses says, "May the bolts of your gate be iron and bronze, and may your strength match your days."

Then Moses is done naming tribes and comes back to the LORD: there is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your aid. The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.

cards.question: With the everlasting arms underneath Israel, Moses says God drives out the ___ before them.

cards.text: In the junk drawer, friend, all I had underneath me was a stack of old takeout menus. Israel gets the everlasting arms.

cards.question: With God driving out the enemy, Moses says Israel dwells ___ in a land of grain and new wine.
Moses ends with a shout: Blessed are you, O Israel, who is like you? What does Moses call Israel?

answers.text: A people saved by the LORD

cards.question: Moses says the LORD is the shield that protects Israel and the sword they boast in.

cards.text: Their enemies will cower before them, Moses says. And that's where the blessing ends, friend, but trust me, Moses' story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats what card 3 just answered ('Surely You love the people') and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, so it is a recap and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'Those words are the ___ that Moses gave us' is in Papa Dorin's own narration, not in quotation marks or clearly given to Moses. The 'us' puts Papa Dorin among the Israelites who received the law.

rule.text: He never says he was there, saw it or knew anyone in it.

findings.problem: The blank tests the exact wording of Deut 33:7 ('may You be a help against his foes'). 'Help,' 'judge' and 'wall' all fit the setup equally well, so the baker can only guess which word Moses used. Nothing in the setup lets them reason it out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says Benjamin is shielded by God all day long and rests upon His shoulders, then asks how he rests. That setup rules out both wrong answers ('Uneasy' and 'Restless'), and those two answers mean nearly the same thing. The right answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage: Ephraim and Manasseh are Joseph's two sons, each with a tribe named after him. It gives no reference for it (for example Gen 41:51-52) and cites only Deut 33:17.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The setup describes tearing off an arm or a head, which leaves 'A timid one' unbelievable as an answer. The retelling also moves the tearing from Gad onto the lion. The text reads 'He lies down like a lion and tears off an arm or a head,' so the 'like' comparison isn't kept as written.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the everlasting arms from Deut 33:27, which card 14 already told. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
